definition.title: Calculus
definition.para: A calculus is a pair (ℒ, ℛ) where ℒ is a formal language — a set of well-formed expressions generated by a grammar over a specified alphabet of logical and non-logical symbols — and ℛ is a set of inference rules that specify, for each rule, a finite collection of premiss sequents and a conclusion sequent. The calculus is identified with its derivability relation ⊢: two presentations of the same calculus are identified if and only if they derive the same sequents over the same language. A sequent is an expression Γ ⊢ Δ where Γ and Δ are finite multisets of formulas of ℒ; the sequent is read as asserting that the conjunction of the formulas in Γ entails the disjunction of the formulas in Δ.
